title: Renormalization group ontology in quantum foundations: a non-interacting spin-0 toy model
abstract: A realist, anti-psi interpretation of quantum field theory is introduced, based on an expanded ontology that was inspired by the renormalization group. A goal will be to work with a classical non-interacting scalar field "toy model" in the canonical ensemble and show that an observer in this expanded ontology, under certain limiting conditions, will see a QFT. The inverse renormalization group (IRG) will be key in both interpreting this expanded ontology and furnishing novel examples of QFTs. This will lead to a definition of Planck's constant that flows as we head towards a fixed point, is expressed in terms of a temperature, and depends on the observer being studied in this expanded ontology. Our hope is that this approach will lead both to insights into quantum foundations and to prescriptions for developing new QFTs.
summary: This theoretical paper proposes a novel, realist interpretation of QFT based on the Renormalization Group. It uses a classical scalar field toy model to show how an observer integrating out different energy scales can perceive an emergent QFT. The work is significant for its attempt to unify quantum foundations with the mathematical structure of RG flow.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a realist, anti-psi interpretation of Quantum Field Theory (QFT) by building an expanded ontology inspired by the Renormalization Group (RG). It seeks to show how emergent QFT can arise from a classical system under specific limiting conditions.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the consistency of RG and Infrared Renormalization Group (IRG) operations can be maintained by carefully tuning parameters, suggesting that the RG flow might act like a group structure.
method: The approach uses a classical non-interacting scalar field 'toy model' in the canonical ensemble, applying RG and IRG procedures across a hierarchy of energy/momentum cutoffs.
model_or_system: The model is a non-interacting scalar field, initially treated classically in a 3D, canonical ensemble. The analysis involves defining nested observers at different points along the RG flow.
key_observables: Planck's constant ($\hbar$), the speed of light ($c$), and the partition function ($Z$) under different observer perspectives.
important_parameters: Energy/momentum cutoffs ($\Lambda, \Lambda_1, \Lambda'$), temperature, and the fixed point parameters.
main_assumptions: The model is highly constrained by using a non-interacting scalar field, and the connection between classical and quantum descriptions relies on specific postulates and limiting procedures.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the RG ontology, applies it to a classical toy model, derives procedures (P1, P2, P3) to connect to QFT, and finally performs calculations to check the commutation of RG and IRG operations.
why_interesting: While focused on QFT foundations, the deep reliance on RG flow, scale separation, and the emergence of effective theories connects conceptually to how effective Hamiltonians are derived in many-body physics.
